alignments.note: אֵי לָזֹאת is a contiguous interrogative expression the ASV renders by the single word *How*, so its three morphemes share one unit under rule 30, headed on אֵי, which carries the wh-lexeme, exactly as תַּחַת מֶה → *Wherefore* heads on מֶה at JER.5.19. Rule 30 names this shape: the whole expression is one unit 'rather than one rendered morpheme beside others marked unrepresented', and its disclaimer that such an expression need not be idiomatic is general rather than local to its noun example. The competing reading, which this verse first carried, splits it under rule 2 and leaves לְ and זֹאת unrepresented on the ground that the English word does not carry their sense; that is rule 35's test for fusion across distance, and בְּיַד → *by* and מִפְּנֵי → *because of* show a contiguous expression fusing a lexeme the English drops.

Finite verb with subject pronoun and modal under rule 17. The fronted *can* stays with the verb: אֵי has an English word of its own, so it is not the yes-or-no particle that takes a question auxiliary.
Bare English object 'thee' leaves the preposition nothing (rule 40).
Suffix to the object pronoun 'thee'.
Suffix to 'thy'.
Noun to 'children'.
Finite verb with auxiliary.
Suffix to 'me'.
Waw to 'and'.
Finite verb to 'sworn'.
בְּ to 'by'.
Negative to 'no'.

לֹא אֱלֹהִים recast as 'them that are no gods'; the supplied antecedent and relative join the substantive's own unit under rule 46 and the copula joins the predicate under rule 20, headed on the lexeme-bearing 'gods'. Discontinuous around the negative (rule 25).
Waw rendered by the temporal connective 'When'; rule 14's list is read off the ASV.

Hiphil שָׂבַע rendered 'had fed ... to the full'; 'fed' is a full lexical verb rather than a bleached light verb, so the head stays on it. Reading 'to the full' as a rule 44 complement would head on 'full'. Discontinuous around the object pronoun (rule 25).
Object marker with a bare English object (rule 16).
Suffix to 'them'.
The ASV writes no connective before 'they committed adultery'; the one written 'and' stands before 'assembled' and belongs to the following waw.
Verb rendered as light verb plus complement, 'committed adultery'; head on the complement (rule 44).
Waw to 'and'.
Accusative of place: the supplied 'at' belongs to the noun whose case-function licenses it (rule 33), and the supplied 'the' determines the construct phrase (rule 29). Discontinuous around 'harlots'.
Nomen rectum rendered by the possessive 'harlots' (rules 19, 28).
Hithpael rendered 'assembled themselves in troops'; the reflexive realizes the verb's own voice (rule 44) and the head stays on the lexical verb.

review_notes: WLC.JER.5.7.v002 is underdetermined and resolved to r00-base for s004; the ASV footnote 'Or, according to another reading, made them swear' records the alternative, which does not alter the token count and so does not engage rule 53.

Chapter reconciliation: אֵי לָזֹאת (s001–s003) is now one unit on *How* under rule 30, matching תַּחַת מֶה → *Wherefore* at JER.5.19. לָ (s002) and זֹאת (s003) are no longer `unrepresented`; the verse falls from 25 units to 23.
All 25 source and 38 target tokens are partitioned exactly once.
